# 1 Enoch Chapter 65 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Ge'ez MS | **Section:** Book of Parables

---

**65:1** And after this Enoch was hidden, and none of the children of men knew where he was hidden, and where he abode, and what had become of him.

**65:2** And his activities had to do with the Watchers, and his days were with the holy ones.

**65:3** And I, Enoch, was blessing the Lord of Majesty and the King of the ages, and behold — the Watchers called me, Enoch the scribe, and said to me:

**65:4** Enoch, you scribe of righteousness, go and declare to the Watchers of heaven who have left the high heaven, the holy and eternal place, and have defiled themselves with women, and have done as the children of earth do, and have taken wives: You have wrought great destruction on the earth.

**65:5** And you shall have no peace nor forgiveness of sin; and inasmuch as they delight themselves in their children,

**65:6** the murder of their beloved ones they shall see, and over the destruction of their children they shall lament, and shall make supplication unto eternity, but mercy and peace you shall not attain.

**65:7** And Enoch went and said: Azazel, you shall have no peace; a severe sentence has gone forth against you to put you in bonds; and you shall not have toleration nor have any request granted, because of the unrighteousness which you have taught, and because of all the works of godlessness and unrighteousness and sin which you have shown to men.

**65:8** Then I went and spoke to them all together, and they were all afraid, and fear and trembling seized them.

**65:9** And they besought me to draw up a petition for them that they might find forgiveness, and to read their petition in the presence of the Lord of heaven.

**65:10** For from that time onward they could not speak with him nor lift up their eyes to heaven, for shame of their sins for which they had been condemned.

**65:11** Then I wrote out their petition, and the prayer regarding their spirits and their deeds individually, and regarding their requests that they should have forgiveness and length of days.

**65:12** And I went off and sat down at the waters of Dan, in the land of Dan, to the south of the west of Hermon; I read their petition until I fell asleep.

---

*SOPHIA notes: Consensus rendering from EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA. Ch. 65 is an interpolation from the Watcher tradition. 'Azazel' preserved untranslated as a proper name (all three translators agree). 'Scribe of righteousness' is Enoch's formal title. The geography 'south of the west of Hermon' is preserved verbatim — it is a distinctive geographical phrase. Divergences logged in disagreement file.*
